title: FBISE Section A Board Examination Simulator 05 (Articles, Prepositions & Poetic Devices)
subject: english-10

questions.question: Choose the appropriate article: 'He is ___ honest and dedicated officer.'
questions.explanation: 'Honest' begins with a silent 'h' and a vowel phoneme /ɒ/, requiring the indefinite article 'an'.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate article: 'She has enrolled in ___ university in Islamabad.'
questions.explanation: 'University' begins with a consonant glide sound /juː/ (like 'yoo'), thus taking the indefinite article 'a' rather than 'an'.

questions.question: Choose the correct article for acronyms: 'His brother is ___ MBA graduate from a prestigious business school.'
questions.explanation: The abbreviation 'MBA' is pronounced starting with a vowel phoneme /ɛm/, thus requiring the indefinite article 'an'.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate article: 'I met ___ one-eyed beggar near the railway crossing.'
questions.explanation: 'One-eyed' begins with the consonantal labio-velar glide /w/ sound (like 'won'), taking 'a' (e.g., 'a one-eyed man').

questions.question: Select the correct sentence regarding geographical article usage:

options.A: The Himalayas form the northern boundary of South Asia.
options.B: The Mount Everest is the highest mountain peak in the world.
options.C: The Asia is the largest continent on Earth.
options.D: The Lake Saif-ul-Malook is in Kaghan.

questions.explanation: Mountain ranges (chains) take the definite article 'the' ('The Himalayas', 'The Alps'), whereas individual mountain peaks ('Mount Everest', 'K2') do not take an article.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'He is addicted ___ smoking.'
questions.explanation: The adjective 'addicted' takes the dependent preposition 'to'.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'The candidate was accused ___ forgery.'
questions.explanation: The verb 'accused' strictly governs the preposition 'of' ('accused of a crime').

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'I prefer reading classical literature ___ watching television.'
questions.explanation: The verb 'prefer' takes the preposition 'to' (never 'than') when expressing preference between two gerunds or nouns.

questions.question: Identify the figure of speech: 'The cat caught the crazy mouse.'
questions.explanation: The repetition of the identical initial hard /k/ consonant sound in 'cat', 'caught', and 'crazy' exemplifies Alliteration.

questions.question: Identify the figure of speech: 'Life is a dream.'
questions.explanation: 'Life is a dream' directly equates two different concepts without using comparative markers like 'as' or 'like', creating a Metaphor.

questions.question: Identify the figure of speech: 'The sunflowers nodded and smiled at the morning sun.'
questions.explanation: Attributing human voluntary actions ('nodded and smiled') to inanimate flowers is Personification.

questions.question: Identify the figure of speech: 'He fought as bravely as a lion on the battlefield.'
questions.explanation: An explicit comparison between his valor and that of a lion using the comparative word 'as...as' constitutes a Simile.

questions.question: Identify the figure of speech: 'There was a deafening silence in the grand courtroom.'
questions.explanation: 'Deafening silence' pairs two inherently contradictory words together side by side, creating an Oxymoron.

questions.question: Identify the literary device: 'I have reminded you a million times to finish your project.'
questions.explanation: Exaggerating the count to 'a million times' for emphatic or rhetorical impact is Hyperbole.

questions.question: In W.H. Davies' poem 'The Rain', what do the 'rich leaves on top' symbolize?

options.A: The wealthy, privileged classes of society
options.B: The elderly members of the community

questions.explanation: In 'The Rain', the upper leaves that drink rain first and pass droplets to the lower poor leaves symbolize the rich and privileged social class.
